title: Hiring compact ops kit for cross-functional pivots
summary: Compact, pragmatic ops kit to accelerate hires who need to pivot across teams (e.g., infra -> serving runtime, product -> solutions). Emphasis on minimal friction first 30 days, role-lite assessments, shadow rotations, and a quiet "week-zero" launch for remote hires.
body:
Purpose: give hiring managers and people-ops a one-page, low-friction kit for fast cross-functional hires. These are folks moving between disciplines (eg backend infra -> serving-runtime, product -> solutions) or when a team needs a mid-cycle headcount pivot. This doc is intentionally lightweight: checklists, micro-assessments, and reusable templates.

Audience: hiring managers doing cross-discipline adds, people-ops partners, hiring-panel members, mentors.

Key principles: keep early signals concrete; reduce setup friction; preserve learning bandwidth; protect sprint capacity with a structured 7-30-90 plan; prefer short live shadowing over long take-home tasks.

What this kit contains (quick):
- Preboarding pack (accounts, role brief, must-reads)
- 72hr quiet launch flow (week-zero)
- Micro-assessment: 60–90 minute evidence session (shadow + paired debugging)
- Shadow rotation schedule (5-day micro-rotation template)
- Interview rubric tuned for cross-functional transfers (collab, systems thinking, product sense, ramp potential)
- Mentor/owner playbook for first 30 days
- Slack/onboarding templates and calendar snippets

Notes to self / open questions:
- Should we require a short take-home for senior ICs? lean towards no, prefer a paired session.
- Budget for buddy time: propose 0.25 FTE first 2 weeks. Need approval from finance.

Preboarding pack (short):
- short role brief (1–2 pages): context, why role shifted, top 3 immediate goals, 90-day success signal
- success metrics the hiring manager will track (top 3)
- git/repos and readme links + who to ping for infra access
- a safe-path checklist: list of low-risk first PRs or docs to update

72hr quiet launch flow (week-zero):
- Day -2: HR email + welcome doc + equipment/cellphone/meeting invites; manager sends role brief
- Day -1: IT/infra automated account setup; People-ops verifies key accesses (github, jira, slack, gcp accounts)
- Day 0: Quiet intro: 30m manager welcome, 60m team async intro thread (no heavy meetings), assign buddy
- Days 1–3: paired shadowing only, no deliverable expectations, 2 x 1hr sync with manager across the period

Micro-assessment (rationale):
- We need a quick but evidence-rich check for domain transfer. Instead of a long take-home, run a 75-minute session: 10m intro, 30–35m paired problem (live repo / debugging / design sketch), 20–25m behavioral and ramp discussion. Score on rubric below.

5-day shadow rotation template (example):
- Day 1: Read core docs + watch 1 recorded oncall handoff; paired read of a recent PR
- Day 2: Pair on a small fix (non-blocking) with mentor; write retrospective note in onboarding doc
- Day 3: Observe triage meeting; own a small follow-up task (doc update)
- Day 4: Lead a 20m sync on findings; pair on rollout checklist
- Day 5: Present 10m summary to manager and mentor; set 30-day goals

Mentor playbook (first 30d):
- Week 0: establish communication norms, pair 2–3 hours/day first 3 days
- Week 1–2: reduce pairing to 3–4 hours total/week; ensure 1 small owned task
- Weeks 3–4: shift to async check-ins; review 30-day milestone and set 60-day outcomes

Hiring manager checklist (pre-hire):
- confirm top-3 success signals and 90d goals
- identify mentor and block buddy calendar for first 10 days
- add micro-assessment owner and panel
- add required accesses list to preboarding pack

Communication templates (short examples to copy):
- Manager welcome DM (Slack): "hi {name}, excited to have you. Quick intro: your first week will be quiet/paired. I will host a 30m intro on day0 at 10am PT. Buddy: {buddy}. If anything blocked, DM me anytime."
- Team async intro thread: include role context, immediate goals, and a pointer to one non-sensitive repo to look at first.

Operational guardrails:
- No heavy project ownership in first 14 days.
- Limit interviews for active candidates to 2 live sessions + micro-assessment
- Encourage hiring panels to include at least one member from the target discipline and one from origin discipline when relevant

Attachment list to add to a drive folder for each hire: short role brief, must-reads markdown, mentor checklist, copyable Slack templates, calendar invites (week-zero and 5-day shadow), micro-assessment guide, rubric as single-sheet.
checklist: Mentor assigned and buddy calendar blocked
Preboarding pack assembled and links verified
IT/Access ticket created 5 business days before start
Onboarding drive folder created and shared
interview_rubric: Collaboration & Communication: ability to ask clarifying Qs, share assumptions, incorporate feedback
Systems reasoning: explain tradeoffs, identify failure modes, propose mitigations
Practicality & ramp potential: chooses approaches likely to ship quickly and learns gaps rapidly
Ownership fit: evidence of shipping with limited scaffolding in prior roles
Cross-discipline empathy: ability to translate between source and target domain language
Cultural signals: transparency about unknowns, receptivity to feedback
micro_assessment_instructions: 35m: paired exercise on a small repo issue or design sketch
Recording: optional, panel agrees in advance
Scoring: each rubric line scored 1–4; hiring manager collates
adoption_notes: Try as a pilot with 6 hires in Q1: three infra->serving pivots, three product->solutions. Track metrics: time-to-first-PR, 30-day autonomy signal, hiring-manager satisfaction. Retro after cohort to tighten mentor FTE assumptions.
